observations.claim: Loading state is three flat grey bars in a single card rather than a skeleton that mirrors the booking card, and no HsSkeletonBlock/shimmer is used — it reads as a broken card, not as loading.
The card can render two full-width HsPrimaryButtons back to back (track/view-status and rate) so there is no single dominant action.

Primary and secondary buttons stacked in the same action column have different fixed heights (HsPrimaryButton is space16 = 64dp, HsSecondaryButton is space12 = 48dp), producing a visibly uneven button stack.
Every ON_RESUME triggers a full refresh which resets state to Loading, so returning to the tab replaces the whole list with the grey placeholder card.
Four consecutive InfoLine rows share the same 18dp icon, bodyMedium size and onSurfaceVariant colour, so date, time, address and payment method have zero hierarchy between them.
StatusPill uses a hardcoded light-amber pair that is not theme-aware; against the dark background #071511 the #F2E7CF pill becomes a bright block.
No booking card carries any imagery — no service thumbnail, no technician avatar — despite the app shipping service hero art.
Empty state offers no CTA back into the catalogue; the only interactive control on the empty screen is the refresh icon.
Screen uses five unmapped M3 slots (headlineSmall, titleMedium x3, labelMedium) which fall back to Roboto, mixing typefaces with the Geist-mapped titleLarge and bodyMedium on the same card.
Zero animation on the screen: no shimmer, no card enter transition, no state cross-fade between Loading/Ready/Error.

Complaint status is matched on raw uppercase server strings with a silent default, so any new backend status renders the generic default copy.

observations.claim: The card's primary title renders the raw backend reasonCode (e.g. 'SERVICE_QUALITY') even though fully localized reason labels already exist in the sibling screen.
The date line prints the raw ISO-8601 createdAt string from the DTO with no formatting at all.
The back button has a null contentDescription and is force-sized to 44dp, so it is both unlabelled for screen readers and under the minimum touch target.
Ten hardcoded pastel/ink colour literals drive the status chips, bypassing the theme entirely, so the chips do not adapt to dark mode.

Tapping a card passes complaint.id into a callback typed bookingId, which the nav graph feeds to ComplaintRoutes.route(bookingId) and the detail screen then uses as a bookingId for loadStatus — the detail screen is therefore keyed on the wrong identifier.
Error state is a bare red sentence with no title, no icon and no explanatory copy, and the sentence is a raw exception message.
List loading is a single centred spinner instead of skeleton rows, so the layout jumps from empty screen to full list.
The empty state offers no action and uses a sad-face icon, framing 'you have no complaints' as a negative rather than a neutral or positive state.
The UI layer consumes the network DTO ComplaintResponseDto directly, which is why raw codes and timestamps leak into the visual layer.

Card corner radius 16dp is off the design-system radius scale (4/8/12/20), and the chip uses RoundedCornerShape(50) percent rather than the `full` token, so this screen's shapes differ from the 20dp cards on the bookings screen.
items() is called without a key, so list diffing and animation are position-based.

loading.quality: Two independent bare spinners — one inside the gradient hero, one in a 160dp empty box where the ledger will be. No skeleton rows, so the page height jumps when data lands.

empty.quality: One line of grey text, no icon, no title, no CTA — the weakest empty state in the cluster and the one a brand-new customer is most likely to see.

Best-behaved error handling in the cluster, but the two retry buttons are styled differently (translucent vs filled).

i18n.hindiRisk: The ledger row is a three-column Row (icon tile, weighted text column, amount) with no minimum width reserved for the amount (lines 242-281); a two-line Hindi reason plus a long amount such as '₹1,29,999.00' will compress the amount column. The hero balance uses displaySmall ExtraBold on a single line (lines 227-231) with no maxLines guard. INFERRED.
i18n.currencyFormatting: formatInr at lines 228 and 278 -> CurrencyFormat.kt:23-26. Correct rupee glyph and Indian lakh grouping via Locale("en","IN"), but fraction digits are always shown so the hero balance reads '₹500.00' rather than '₹500', and numerals stay Latin under the Hindi locale. The ledger date formatter is pinned to Locale.ENGLISH (lines 327-330), so dates render as '12 Jul 2026, 3:05 pm' even in Hindi, and it falls back to echoing the raw ISO string if parsing fails (line 332).

observations.claim: The ledger empty state is a single line of grey text with no icon, title or CTA — and it is the state every new customer sees, since a fresh account has no credits.
The ledger row's primary label is entry.reason, a raw server-supplied string with no localization path, so Hindi users see whatever English text the backend wrote.
The ledger date formatter is hardcoded to Locale.ENGLISH, so month names and am/pm never localize.
Both loading states are bare spinners, and the hero loading box is 100dp tall versus a taller loaded hero, so the layout visibly jumps when the balance arrives.
Credit/debit amount colours and the hero gradient's second stop are hardcoded literals that do not adapt to the dark palette.
Ledger rows have full card styling (clip, surface fill, 1dp border) but no click handler, so they read as tappable and are not — even though the entry carries a bookingId to drill into.
The hero balance always renders two decimal places, e.g. '₹500.00', because formatInr uses the default currency fraction digits — noisy for a headline number in a whole-rupee product.
The ledger date is forced to 11sp, smaller than any mapped type slot, on a screen whose target users skew older and rural.
The two retry buttons on the same screen are styled differently — a 20%-alpha translucent button in the hero and a solid primary button in the ledger — so the same action has two visual identities.
Hero, section header and ledger rows use three different left insets (16dp, 20dp, 16dp with a further 14dp inner) so no vertical alignment line runs down the screen.
The hero balance uses displaySmall, an unmapped M3 slot, so the single most prominent number on the screen renders in Roboto while the rest of the screen uses the mapped Geist slots.
REFUND uses an Add icon and CREDIT_APPLIED uses a Remove icon, so the ledger's iconography is arithmetic symbols rather than semantic imagery.
